rationale: The deployed model under-called benign lesions as 'normal' (test benign recall 0.733; 4 of 4 errors were lesion-called-normal, the clinically dangerous direction). A normal-class penalty was tuned by StratifiedGroupKFold cross-validation over train+val (85 benign examples) rather than on the 157-image validation split alone, which contains only 15 benign images and could not resolve the threshold. Selection required malignant recall to not regress and normal recall to stay >= 0.90.
tradeoff: Normal recall falls ~5 points: more healthy scans are flagged for review. For a screening-support tool this is the correct direction - a false alarm costs a follow-up read, a missed lesion costs far more.
caveats: The cross-validation objective curve was nearly flat (0.985 vs 0.984 across the sweep), so the exact weight is weakly determined; the validation constraint check is what confirmed it.
Based on 15 benign validation and 15 benign test images. Confidence intervals are wide.
This is a decision-threshold change, not a better-trained model. The real fix is more benign training data.
